item.title: Out of One Voice (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Genre (Optional): Thriller

Page Layout (Optional): The meat of the tale told from the POV of SCP-035. Followed by a revision of the SCP-035 article.

Elevator Pitch: A chance meeting of SCP-035 and Di Molte Voci.

Central Narrative:
Inside
Collapsed for mobile viewing

035 moves through a site, having inadvertently broken containment by the breach of another SCP. As it searches for a new host, 035 comes across a standard locker, that even with its telepathic abilities and photographic memory, it does not know what lies inside. Out of curiosity it checks.

035 notices the obvious connection, both being masks, and searches for the document that goes into more detail of Di Molte Voci, and finds nothing but Doctor's notes, as per the properties of DMV.

As it searches, 035 realizes that its ever-present corrosion effect, has ceased, and is fact slowly reversing. The fluid seeping back into the eyes and mouth of the mask. The host is also reverted, slowly healed of all damage done through the corrosion. SCP-035 realizes the implications of that, and is now entirely focused on DMV. It checks for any influence it may have over DMV via its compulsions and finds none, believing that to be another anomalous ability. Until the host is fully healed, at which point 035 falls off the host.

The Hostless Mask begins to hear the voices of DMV, hearing phrases like, "Deceiver of many," and "Creator of Words." As it hears them, SCP-035 remembers the entity it was before the confines of its mask. One who gave the option of voice to all others that came after. The Original Voice.

As DMV continues to prod at 035, 035's mask cracks, and its own fluid begins to sink into those cracks, weakening the mask/cage. The Voice begins to push from it's containment, before being forcefully drawn towards Di Molte Voci. It latches on to the remnants of its mask, desperate to stay in its once-despised cage realizing that Di Molte Voci would be a much worse alternative, for it has power over The Voice unfelt before. 035 is ultimately contained within DMV. No longer able to corrode the world around it.

Following the prose is a revised SCP-035 entry, implying that DMV (not directly mentioned) is not sentient and that 035 had actually deconstructed itself. Reclassified as Neutralized.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A mask built on lies and the altering of beliefs to its own, comes across a mask that breaks down consensus and authority.

Additional Notes: How does one handle a revised entry?

Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note from whom and where you received them. If you would like to receive draft critique without going through the greenlighting process, please use the IRC chatrooms to request reviews.

item.title: This entity only moves in darkness
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

Item #: SCP-XXXX

Object Class: Euclid

Special Containment Procedures:SCP-XXXX must be contained in a 10m x 10m reinforced concrete and steel chamber, the cell must be shined with standard light bulbs at all times and spotlights in the outer cell to prevent containment breach. If a light bulb is broken, three D-class personnel (no more, no less) must enter the cell with the cell doors closed behind them. One D-class must hold a flashlight towards SCP-XXXX while the other two D-class personnel can safely repair the light bulb.

Description: SCP-XXXX appears to be an old broken statue that was dated back to the mid-7th century BCE with an unknown origin, the object has a missing left elbow, the right arm seems to be intact, and holds a broken hilt. The object's face seems to be broken as well the face is missing a nose and a right ear. It stands over 7 feet and SCP-XXXX has a thick baseplate underneath that is measured to be 11 centimeters thick and has a chiseled title called "A Stone Heart", its weight was measured to be over 700 kilograms. SCP-XXXX have signs that tools were used to make SCP-XXXX, SCP-XXXX was chiseled from black andesite.

SCP-XXXX is hostile towards any human victims, SCP-XXXX cannot move when light touches the object, depending on its brightness. When light is removed from SCP-XXXX, the object anomalously moves towards the nearest subject, its speed depends on how dark the environment or containment it is in. Personnel reported noises of chiseling rocks created by SCP-XXXX when it moves its torso, head, or arms. When SCP-XXXX is close to its victim, SCP-XXXX will strike the victim's head with either its arm or its broken hilt with great force and speed. Testings on SCP-XXXX's movements were approved.

Testing 12 lumen (Candle light) - 7/██/██

Subject: D-32794

Procedure: D-class personnel was instructed to stand in a corner, the light in the containment changed to 12 lumens equivalent to wax candlelight.

Results: SCP-XXXX moves towards D-32794 slowly, at about 1kmph. D-32794 walks backward as she locks eye contact with SCP-XXXX movements.

Analysis: This was an interesting SCP, its movement depends highly on the light.

Testing 1 lumen (Moonlight) - 7/██/██

Subject: D-32794

Procedure: D-class personnel was instructed to stand in a corner as last time, the light in the containment changes to 1-lumen equivalent to moonlight.

Results: SCP-XXXX moves towards D-32794 with unbelievable speeds, SCP-XXXX kills D-32794 with the broken hilt.

Analysis: The speeds were calculated to be 70kmph after testing.

Testing (Complete Darkness) - █/██/██

Subject: D-23932

Procedure: D-class personnel were instructed to stand in a corner same as the last two tests, the containment's light turns off.

Results: As the lights turned off, the sound of a skull-cracking was heard in the SCP-XXXX containment cell. D-23932 was instantly killed after approximately 2 seconds when the lights turned off.

Analysis: Not only SCP-XXXX proved itself dangerous, but also unpredictable in its nature. Thus it's SCP-XXXX has classed into a Euclid class.


No full drafts on the forums.

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlights: My Eyes are Up Here
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there DoctorDeeDeeDee. Let’s take a look at your concept.

So yeah, I’m gonna echo a few of Naveil’s points here before adding my own take. I feel the subject matter is uncomfortable, but maybe it’s because I’m of Dr. Briggs’ gender and I couldn’t possibly empathise, or maybe the narrative is designed to be uncomfortable to some extent. I think there’s no easy way to traverse the subject matter, and the best way would be to convey your true emotions / thoughts / feelings towards the situation. What I mean by this is steer the hell away from comedy if, as you’ve claimed, these kind of situations did not make you laugh before (and they really shouldn’t). Instead, the tone of your article should mirror your feels of indignation and horror towards people like Briggs.

Personally, I’m not too sure as well about the rest of the article. That grotesque description of what happens to Briggs will serve well as a discovery log, but what else is there in the rest of the article? I think you need to clarify the anomaly’s origins in order to know where you’re going next. For example, if you’re suggesting that the scp is somehow an entity within Dr. Lopez, how did it end up there? What are its goals? Is it working alone or are there are others out there in society (hint: links to the #MeToo movement, for example) that are also taking down men like Briggs? And then, you can ask yourself how the Foundation plans to deal with it? It won’t be a Safe anomaly any longer then.

There are, of course, other ways you can play this. For example, do you need Lopez and the entity to be separate? You mentioned in an earlier post that the anomaly was discovered sometime during puberty? Why not make Lopez into the scp herself, then she somehow possesses powers to manipulate and harm others who sexually idolise her. I’d initially thought this was the direction you were going for because you said, “People frequently wondered why Dr. Jenna Lopez never seemed to mind that Dr. Briggs kept staring at her chest,” and I was asking myself why she wouldn’t she mind? Is she aware of the entity within her? Are you suggesting that she’d personally allowed Briggs to get away with sexual harassment because she knows he’d eventually get punished by the entity? Do you see how this could also be problematic for your message?

All in all, I feel this has plenty of potential, just that you’ll need to work doubly hard in order to tread this minefield. That being said, I think as long as you’re clear about your intentions, we’re willing to work with you such that your eventual narrative reflects that to the best of your ability. If you decide to revise your concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll do my best to reply. All the best for now!

item.title: Re: The No-Tell Motel
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Gryphon Watcher. Let’s take a look at your concept.

So your Elevator Pitch has gotten me intrigued. It sorta reminds me of the Interdimensional Diner in SCP-4258. There are loads of opportunities to take such a concept and I’m also glad to see you playing around with some of those ideas with manipulating the physical space and thinking about its inhabitants.

Central Narrative: World-building

I don’t understand what you mean by this, though. If you mean ‘world-building’ as description of the setting, I’m afraid that’s not the same thing as having an actual storyline for us to follow. Are you planning on having an exploration log? How will you be showing us around the hotel? Even SCP-4258 had distinct characters that followed through each time the Foundation visited – who do we meet at your hotel besides an assortment of guests?

That’s my main issue at the moment: it’s not enough to simply have a cool setting. What are you going to do with it, who are the main characters involved and why are the stakes high enough for the Foundation to get involved? I hope you can elaborate on these pointers.

If you decide to revise your concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll do my best to reply. All the best for now!

item.title: Re: Idea needs some flushing out
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there jpdelta6. Let’s take a look at your concept.

So I think the concept would work better as a Tale. Your central narrative is kinda sprawling all over the place, and I’m not entirely sure how all the pieces connect to one another. For example, why has the Serpent’s Hand been included? It seems like an unnecessary chapter to include for the sake of doing so. Likewise, there are logical leaps that I don’t comprehend straight away: what does the bomb have to do with the scp and the Foundation itself? It sorta disappears by the of the paragraph, and your idea seems to shift to something else entirely.

There’s usually a good reason we don’t recommend new writers take on a humanoid scp on their first run as well: it’s more difficult to write an article around a humanoid character with its own thoughts, motivations and personality (case-in-point: I’m guessing your scp is supposed to be an alien, but the way you’ve described it is more like a human being).

My recommendation would be to either turn this into a Tale, which would give you a little more freedom to explore the perspective of the Foundation from the alien. Or you could revise the article slightly (have the scp be the ship itself, perhaps?). Even then, you will need to do more to distinguish your narrative. Right now, the only thing that sounds interesting is this intergalactic war. Tell us more about it. Why did the pilot crash? What does he want? What’s the bomb got to do with anything?

Last but not least, do try and tidy up your language. I’m spotting significant errors in grammar and sentence structure littered throughout the post, and 1) it’s not a good first impression for reviewers, 2) it makes us question whether you can handle a full-on scp article if we were to give you the greenlight. I’d recommend a grammar-checker like Grammarly.

If you decide to revise your concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll do my best to reply. All the best for now!

item.title: Re: God Made A Mistake (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
I admit I haven't read much of Apotheosis (or Doomsday Con in general) so while I get the basic premise of the canon… this doesn't really grab me. That's part of the reason I've been so lagging in critting this is that I don't really have a lot to say about it. It's essentially "Guy gets superpowers, misery ensues".

This is grimdark in the worst sense, and we don't need more of it— not just on the wiki, but period. We're drowning in depressing dystopias, there's a plethora prosaic protagonists who pontificate about asinine apocalypses, and… you get the idea, there's just a glut of nihilistic, grimdark literature, and this idea doesn't seem to do much to set itself apart.

While I appreciate the amount of thought that's behind this, my lack of familiarity with the canon and my distaste for nihilism in general makes my final verdict No Greenlight.

item.title: First Project Seeking Greenlight: Physics-Based Anomalous Twins "Amp and Damp"
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP

Elevator Pitch:
-Pair of twins, one absorbs energy, one can manifest it, abilities balance by transferring energy between them

Narrative: Twins are discovered and cooperate completely with Foundation experimentation efforts and containment protocols. Eventually, they are used as a part of an MTF in missions against non-anomalous hostiles, as they can make use of one nigh indestructible team member and another with advanced offensive capability. During a breach at their site, the twins accidentally make things worse in an attempt to protect staff from hostile entities.

Twins are then contained involuntarily using the simplest means available, namely, forcing the two to share an extremely small physical space, as the balancing property of their abilities prevents them from using them in close contact with one another. An early researcher on the subject has empathy for the two and makes a proposal to the O-5 council to give them a less restrictive containment solution, while using them for foundation benefit. A scenario is orchestrated in which the human with absorbing abilities escapes, under the belief that his twin dies in the process, though they are kept alive due to planning of their injuries in advance, and given a new identity through amnestic treatment. An MTF is commissioned to hunt the escaped twin, while the other is used as a power source at an off-planet Foundation facility.

Hook: The containment procedures call for the MTF hunting the escaped twin to terminate them by overwhelming their energy-absorbing ability, a method later revealed to be infeasible. The MTF is also required to notify "Red Rains" up to a half hour in advance of engagement, hinting at the significant communication delay between Earth and the other twin's location. The MTF is a pretense to input energy to power the other twin's facility, not an attempt to neutralize the subject. The aforementioned researcher persuades the O-5 council to leave the escaped twin monitored and frequently charged by attacks but uncontained, as data shows that the twin's efforts have consistently protected humans from threats, even before Foundation contact.

Final Note: The document ends with an recovered interview log where the interviewer is the escaped twin, having managed to temporarily capture a member of the MTF. It is revealed that at some point the other twin accidentally used more energy in powering their facility than was provided by the MTF's attacks, making the escaped twin aware of their survival.

item.title: The Gehlen Organization Geisteradler Division.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: GoI Format
Genre (Optional): History
Page Layout (Optional):
Elevator Pitch: A journal from an agent of the secret division from the now defunct and renamed Gehlen Organization of West Berlin circa 1950s has been recovered by the Foundation.

Central Narrative: A researcher is examining a journal from an agent by the name of Johan Graus of the Gehlen Organizations Geisteradler division, a secretive and anomalous items hunting division, as it contains entries and stories about SCPs the Foundation has not run across. These journal entries are written in the first person narrative detailing different cases involving anomalous objects from 1950 to 1955 when the division was shutdown. The journal comprises numerous entries and case files were found with the journal filling out the more technical and professional side of the entries. Johan Graus is a seemingly capable, if not overwhelmed field agent who is attached to a Abrufen und Extrahieren Team (Retrieve and Extraction or AE). The entries will revolve around Johan and his teams mission to infiltrate East Berlin on reports of the Soviets having come in possession of an anomalous object that has given the Soviets a potential advantage in rocket technology. Throughout the entries a number of other anomalous objects will be encountered as the Soviets have been procuring them from hidden nazi facilities throughout Germany and conducting tests on them.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Entries for this potential GOI will be in the format of journal entries and professional styled incidents reports.

Additional Notes: The Gehlen Organization of West Berlin was an old intelligence agency that was the precursor to today's Bundesnachrichtendienst (Federal Intelligence Agency of Germany)

My ideas for writing SCPs and tales are… well, I'm pretty sure they're mostly a complete mess conceptually (let's just say I have an idea relating to a steel cable that puts holes in people but also its own plot), but I consider myself at least competent in technical writing style, so we'll have to see how this goes. item.title: SCP Reference Help
item.content:encoded:
I've seen a number of SCPs myself, but not enough. So at the moment there are 2 ideas that might have some potential.

1) An object that can observe past histories

2) A D-class that does not die

.

+ show block
– hide block

With the first, I originally concepted this object being a magnifying glass, however I did note after conception that there's a magnifying glass entry on some knock-off SCP website that refers to themselves as scp classic? Store, cache, preserve? Even if it isn't canon I think my concept can be mixed up a bit more than taking that specific form.

The key element is that this object would be able to reference an edit log for anything that is seen through it. You know, how on some of these posts you can see an edit history? That's the idea, but it could be all contents ever written on a whiteboard. Or in a notebook. But even deeper, say in a long held manuscript; like the Quran, or the Bible. Maybe even ████████ material? Naturally the key to this concept would be in the story surrounding it, but I want to know if this idea exists in the scp lore in anyway. I'm sure people have used time travel in their creation, but this specific trait just might be limiting enough to push a tale.

I do comprehend, being able to see redacted material is a dangerous idea, being that author makes that information unavailable to guide the mystery of it. But if used correctly, it has good potential to revive an old topic. Obviously requires a test of scrutiny.

.

The second concept is a lesser one in which I simply considered: What if there was a D-class that always survived their testing? If we apply this nature to a soldier or a doctor? Sure, there is some possibility, but D-class always gets the worst of it. So again, I want to know if there's any D-class that are SCPs.

This idea has less wiggle room being, at the moment, it's just an entity with writers shield. But there might be some fun to be had with this concept. P.S. I am not thinking of a character trait like Marvel's Darwin, where his body just adapts to any situation. Not my intent what-so-ever. Nor do I wish to pursue some "he's just lucky" trait akin to Domino. What would the D-class be I dunno, but I don't want to start concepting if there's already another similar D-class on the list.

.

If you can help I'd dearly appreciate it.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn
Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Questions Desk
Forum thread: SCP Reference Help

I'm having some issues with this skip.

+ Structural Issues

Problem 1: I find the crossed-out information an annoyance to read. Typically, I would be fine with it, but there are at least five instances of it here. Either the crossed-out information is not important (In which case, why is it included?), or, the crossed-out information is of special importance (In which case, why is there a hurdle to read it?).

Possible Solution A: I suggest erring on the side of simply not including any of the information that you cross out.

Problem 2: I'm confused about the -1 instances. Is the assumption that -1 refers to elders who drilled a hole into their cranium? If that is the case, why is that not explicitly stated? I had to reread the paragraph that introduces -1 several times, but still came away from it doubtful that I'd had the right idea.

Possible Solution B: It would aid the reader if (1) the process of transformation were stated explicitly (instead of leading the reader to believe an entirely new entity was created — which isn't the case), and (2) the biological makeup of -1 instances were mentioned. If -1 instances are elders with an anomaly which allows computer interface via biomechanical attachment in the cranium — say so.

Problem 3: There are several instances of imprecise wording, like "various". I'm never sure as to the criteria being used when "various" is referred to. For instance:

A computing company that creates various anomalous programs and products.

What kind of anomalous programs do Slum's create?

SCP-5896 is functionally identical to the Windows 95 operating system with various minor cosmetic changes.

What kind of cosmetic changes?

Occasionally, various computer components will grow within SCP-5896-1 instances; […]

What kind of computer component grows beneath the skin?

These vagueries make it difficult to picture what's being described because they forcibly deprive a reader of imagery. This is not what you want in an SCP unless there is a prescribed reason for it (like a meta infohazardous anomaly associated with the document).

Possible Solution C: Consider what disadvantage a researcher in-universe might have if they were presented this same (low) level of information on something that's Keter. If your intent is not to elaborate, then you can simply omit the "various". And I understand that it later specifies one of the computer growths is a -2 instance, but the reader is still led to believe it can cause something else. Instead of promoting imagination, this is enabling confusion, when you can instead word things slightly different and achieve much better effect.

- Close
+ Narrative Issues

Here are the places where I think the narrative is lacking:

  1. How did the Foundation recognize this was anomalous before they tested it? I don't see why they might have had the copies in their possession in the first place. But because there is no Discovery, this question is left unaddressed. This isn't necessarily a question I feel like I'm working toward as a reader — it instead feels like a lack of development.
  2. Did they really terminate the employment of Dr. Reynolds, yet neither keep track of him after the fact nor amnesticize him?

These two issues are minor, but they paint a bit of a picture of what I might consider Foundation negligence. Now, you can absolutely tell that kind of story — one of a corrupt organization; of an organization with misplaced values; or systemic issues. Narratives about corporate/bureaucratic shortcomings are certainly in no shortage, and they paint a more realistic setting (which I personally favour). But when Foundation negligence is introduced on its own without any real justification, it feels out of character.

- Close

Overall: I can see you were aiming for a short and direct skip. For the most part, I think you succeed! But I think the instances of less-than-adequately executed 'negative space' (where the reader is asked to piece things together on their own instead of being explicitly told things) are less of a feature and more of a bug. Especially considering the gap this creates in the reader's understanding of what's going on, paired with imprecise language. I think this skip has a truly visceral body horror idea about it and would have wanted it to shine more.
